function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **nodejs‑welcome** repository.  
It contains:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight container for the Node.js app |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` | Deployment + Service definition for Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow that builds & pushes the image on every push to `main` |

> **NOTE** – The repository is a Node.js project, so the Docker image is based on `node:14‑alpine`.  
> If you prefer a different Node version, simply change the `FROM` line.

---

## 1️⃣  Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – Alpine‑based Node 14 (small footprint)
FROM node:14-alpine

# Working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies only
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["npm", "start"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * Uses an official Node image → no need to install Node manually.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees reproducible installs.  
> * Only production deps are installed → smaller image.  
> * `EXPOSE 3000` matches the default port used by the sample app.

---

## 2️⃣  Kubernetes YAML

Create a folder called `k8s` (or any name you like) and add `deployment.yaml` inside it.

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_DOCKERHUB_OR_AWS_ECR>/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer   # Change to ClusterIP / NodePort if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # External port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> **What to replace?**  
> * `<YOUR_DOCKERHUB_OR_AWS_ECR>` – the registry where you’ll push the image.  
> * `replicas` – adjust based on expected load.  
> * `type` – `LoadBalancer` gives you an external IP; use `ClusterIP` for internal‑only services.

---

## 3️⃣  GitHub Actions Workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` and add `ci.yml`.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # Set up Node.js
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      # Install dependencies
      - name: Install deps
        run: npm ci

      # Run tests (optional – remove if you don't have tests)
      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

      # Build Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .

      # Log in to Docker Hub (or other registry)
      - name: Login to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Push image
      - name: Push Docker image
        run: |
          docker push ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
```

### Secrets you’ll need

| Secret | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` | Your Docker Hub username |
| `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` | A Docker Hub access token (or password) |

> **Tip** – If you’re using AWS ECR or another registry, replace the Docker Hub steps with the appropriate login action (`aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login`, etc.).

---

## 4️⃣  Add, Commit & Push

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo (if you haven’t already)
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome

# 2. Add the new files
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# 3. Commit
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"

# 4. Push
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run on the `main` branch, building the Docker image and pushing it to your registry.

---

## 🎉 Done!

You now have:

* A ready‑to‑build Docker image for the Node.js app.  
* Kubernetes manifests that deploy two replicas behind a LoadBalancer.  
* A CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image whenever you push to `main`.

Feel free to tweak the values (Node version, image tags, replica count, etc.) to suit your environment. Happy coding!
